messages:
maria: Quick probe update — ran a 2h sweep of continuous-batcher with prompt-length buckets + decode-rate bins on rtx-pool. Short summary: decode-rate bucketing reduces p95 for medium prompts but we see unexpected regression for very short prompts when KV prefetch is enabled.

li: Which config did you use for token budget targets?

maria: token_budget_targets = {short:32, mid:64, long:128}, queue_policy = "length_priority", decode_bins = [0-10,11-30,31+], batch_max = 32. KV prefetch = on for short/mid.

mike: Posting profiler dump for one representative regression case (short prompt, 8 tokens). Notice kernel handoff at batch size 16 -> 24.
```
PROFILE: run=1958003456-caseA
avg_latency_ms: 26
p50: 18
p95: 210
p99: 480
batch_sizes: [1:1200, 4:300, 8:180, 16:40, 24:10]
kernel: fast_attention used for <=16, fallback_kernel for >16
KV_prefetch_hits: 0.84
KV_prefetch_overhead_ms: +12ms per request (short prompts)
```

ana: Two thoughts: 1) If kernel selection flips to fallback_kernel at >16 we lose vectorized decode perf — that explains p95 jump. 2) KV prefetch overhead dominates when decode time is tiny (short prompts). Try disabling KV prefetch for short bucket or reducing token_budget_target to avoid large batch formation.

li: Agreed. Also the decode-rate bucketing seems to send fast-decode requests into the same admission queue as slow-decode ones because our current classifier only uses prompt length. Need to add a light-weight decode-rate estimate at admission (first 4 tokens sampling).

sara: I ran a micro-probe where admission checks first-4-token decode-time and routes to low-latency pool if avg < 6ms. Results: p95 short dropped from 210 -> 60, overall throughput unchanged.

mike: That matches kernel hypothesis. If we keep batch_max=32 but cap per-bucket max_batch_for_kernel = 16 for short bucket we avoid kernel fallback while still batching mids/larges. Example config: 
```json
{"buckets": [{"name":"short","len_max":32,"token_budget":32,"max_batch_for_kernel":16,"kv_prefetch":false},{"name":"mid","len_max":128,"token_budget":64,"max_batch_for_kernel":24,"kv_prefetch":true},{"name":"long","len_min":129,"token_budget":128,"kv_prefetch":true}]}
```

maria: Nice. Also saw a perf-bot alert for a regression in kernel compiled waveform on that node, might be related. @perf-bot can you attach the build hash so infra can check kernel selector mapping? :eyes:

perf-bot: Automated note — regression alert 1958003468; kernel-chooser v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 deployed on rtx-cluster at 1958003400, correlated with increased fallback_kernel invocations. See: https://ci.redwood/inference/kernels/1958003400

ana: So action items: (1) temporarily disable KV prefetch for short bucket, (2) add first-4-token decode estimator at admission, (3) set max_batch_for_kernel for short bucket to 16, (4) rollback kernel-chooser to v2.4.1 on rtx-3 for a canary.

li: I'll own (2) and (3). I'll push a probe config: `./run_probe --buckets "len:<32,32-128,>128" --decode-sample 4 --token-targets 32,64,128 --cap-short-batch 16` and iterate.

mike: I'll coordinate the kernel rollback with infra and re-run the profiler after rollback.

maria: Great. Let's reconvene tomorrow after the short-bucket-disabled run (2h). If p95 remains >100ms we'll consider dynamic KV prefetch throttling instead of full disable. :thumbsup:
